frontier.hypothesis: The surviving route to the target's seats on the head-exact chassis is to keep the +6 depth-3 passenger lift on j (nrefs 17, pri 11525, byte-neutral and already measured) and simultaneously lift the three small allocnos that currently sit at ord 12-14 (pri 10000, 10909, 12000) above 11525 with their own byte-neutral passengers, so that the allocation ORDER keeps j at ord 15 where hardreg 12 is the lowest free register.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocates in descending allocno_pri and gives each allocno the lowest free hard register, so a seat is determined by ordinal position, not by priority magnitude. d3 showed that lifting j alone moves it to ord=11 where hardreg 9 is free; the fix is to lift everything that must precede it by the same kind of byte-neutral chain. The (S + P) - P extender is now a measured, byte-neutral, per-variable ref multiplier (+2 per loop-depth level), so the ord ladder is directly programmable.
frontier.next_probe: Identify the variables behind pseudos p130 / p131 / p132 (nrefs 6, livelen 10-12) in tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s20/alloc_h1/stderr.log by cross-referencing the .lreg dump, then sweep depth-3 passenger chains on each so their pri exceeds 11525 while j stays at ord 15. Read the alloc table after EVERY build (the ord column, not the score) and accept only tables whose ord 15 row is j with hardreg 12; build_insns must stay 173. Note that every such chain is an F1 combine-foldable chain-extender and would need a FAKE annotation plus the lever-exhaustion ledger, so if a table lands the seats the correct next step is a ruling-request naming the 2026-07-01 F1 grant, not a candidate-ready.

frontier.hypothesis: The blend arm's 19-insn seat residual (px / g_src / b_src / r_src, s14-s16) is decidable by the newly-isolated ASSIGNMENT-order lever, because its pair is an exact 32727 priority TIE and global.c:654 breaks ties by declaration order - s16 only ever varied declaration sites, never the assignment order that sets livelen.
frontier.mechanism: s14/s16 measured px at nrefs 12 / livelen 11 / pri 32727 tied with r_src, with the tie decided by the lower pseudo number, and found declaration-site renumbering byte-neutral across all 384 spellings. s20 proved livelen is set by assignment order independently of the pseudo number, so ties between the blend arm's carriers can be CREATED (by equalising livelen) and then steered by declaration order - a two-dimensional lattice s16 never explored, worth 19 of the remaining 26 points.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the s16 carrier harness (tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s16/batch_alloc.py, carrier_alloc.json) on the chassis_s20_e4_decl_assign_split_26.c body, this time sweeping the declaration order and the assignment order of pixel / px / r_src / g_src / b_src as TWO independent axes. Filter on the alloc table first: keep only spellings where px and g_src print equal pri (a tie), then check which of them has the lower pseudo, and score only those.

frontier.hypothesis: The 4-insn head residual the incumbent pays can be removed without touching the j / complement pair, by making `dst = dst_buf` ineligible for reorg's backward scan so the blez's slot is filled from the fall-through with j's def instead.
frontier.mechanism: s18's BB2_DBR_DEBUG trace shows the backward scan rejecting trials 128 / 125 / 124 / 394 and accepting insn 121, `addiu a2,sp,1040`. In the target that insn sits at row 57, early in the head, and is NOT used for the slot - so in the original something between it and the branch made it ineligible. Eligibility is decided by refset / setset / setneed on the insn's destination, i.e. by whether $a2 is read or written between the insn and the jump, which is a source-side property of where the dst cursor is initialised and first used.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tools/grinder/dump.ps1 plus the s18 BB2_DBR_DEBUG harness on the INCUMBENT body (s18 traced it on h1) and read the trial list for the blez; then enumerate spellings that put a read or a write of the dst cursor between its initialisation and the guard branch without adding an insn - e.g. initialising dst from a second cursor, or deriving src from dst. s15's 96-form cursor declaration-site sweep only moved the declaration site and never targeted reorg eligibility, so it does not cover this.
